title: Client runtime bootmap wireframe — quickstart draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a working wireframe for a "client runtime" quickstart that focuses on the developer path of integrating Redwood calls into small server-side runtimes (sidecar or embedded client) and local-first dev flows. The goal: a 5-minute smoke, a 15-minute sample integration, and a single-file example that step-by-step demonstrates safe defaults (timeout, retries, telemetry).

Audience:
- Product and platform engineers who embed Redwood into app runtimes
- Solutions engineers doing technical onboarding for early customers
- SDK maintainers who will turn this into an opinionated quickstart + sample app

Success metrics (how we’ll judge this quickstart):
- 5-minute success rate: >= 80% of new users can run the single-file example without env changes
- Time-to-first-call: median < 5 minutes in test run sessions
- Completion of the 15-minute sample app (local->deployed): >= 50% in self-serve cohort
- Telemetry: quickstart emits minimal telemetry (sdk.init, request.start, request.complete, error.rate) for product analytics

High-level flows (three paths):
1) 5-minute single-file smoke (recommended first step)
   - Preconditions: Node 18+ installed, REDWOOD_API_KEY in env
   - Action: run examples/quickstart/run.js which does: import client, call /v1/generate, print response
   - Outcome: Hello/OK response + printed latency and token usage summary

2) 15-minute sample integration (typical embed)
   - Preconditions: basic app (Express/Rails/Go) skeleton
   - Action: add redwood client to dependency, implement a caching + fallback wrapper (local mock -> hosted), add a sample route that uses streaming, add telemetry hooks
   - Outcome: app serves a demo endpoint and includes a README for config and rollout notes

3) Local-first sidecar shim (30–60 minutes)
   - Purpose: demonstrate sidecar pattern for local dev parity when customers run Private/On-prem
   - Action: lightweight containerized shim that proxies requests to Redwood, injects local KV cache for prefixes, records per-request tags
   - Outcome: reproducible dev environment that mirrors dedicated/private networking behaviour

Opinionated defaults (to bake into the sample code and SDK docs):
- request timeout: 15s (override via per-call option)
- retry policy: exponential backoff, max 3 retries for 5xx/network
- streaming: enabled for chat/generation by default when client supports it
- token/cost telemetry: emit aggregated tokens_per_request, model_name, latency_ms, success bool

Example snippets (to be polished for final SDK docs)
- CLI/cURL quick smoke:
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/mini-7b","input":"Hello from Quickstart"}'

- Node minimal (examples/quickstart/run.js)
  // run: REDWOOD_API_KEY=... node run.js
  const Redwood = require('redwood-inference');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, timeout: 15000 });
  (async () => {
    try {
      const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood/mini-7b', input: 'Write a haiku about coffee' });
      console.log(res.output);
      console.log('latency_ms=', res.meta.latency_ms, 'tokens=', res.meta.tokens_total);
    } catch (err) {
      console.error('quickstart error:', err.message);
      process.exit(1);
    }
  })();

Key checklist for the single-file example (packaged as examples/quickstart):
- [ ] one-file runnable example (node/python) with env-driven config
- [ ] clear README -> steps: install, set API key, run, expected output
- [ ] local mock mode: if REDWOOD_API_URL unset, start a tiny in-process mock server that returns canned responses (helps offline demos)
- [ ] telemetry hooks toggled by REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=on|off
- [ ] CI smoke for example (runs on PRs to ensure quickstart stays green)

Telemetry and analytics (minimal set for quickstart):
- sdk.init -> emitted once per process start, includes sdk.version, runtime, env
- request.start -> includes model, route, sample_rate
- request.complete -> duration_ms, status(200/4xx/5xx), tokens_in, tokens_out
- error.event -> error.code, stage (init|request|parse)
Notes: privacy-first — no PII should ever be sent as telemetry. Telemetry should be opt-out for drafts and opt-in by default for OSS examples.

Failure modes & diagnostics included in doc:
- common local errors and remedies: invalid API key, network blocked by corporate proxy, missing Node version
- guidance on falling back to local mock and using request logging for debugging
- sample logs with trace ids that map back to console prints and SDK telemetry events

Rollout and gating plan (how to go from wireframe -> published quickstart):
- Phase 0 (this draft) -> internal review (DX + SDK) -> owner: Ava
- Phase 1 -> create single-file examples in both Node and Python + README -> PR -> CI smoke -> owner: Liam
- Phase 2 -> add Express sample + streaming demo + telemetry -> user-tested with two solutions-eng customers -> owner: Priya
- Phase 3 -> publish to docs.redwood.ai and link from SDK home page; add translations and CLI snippets -> owner: Marco

Open questions / TODOs (to resolve before final publish):
- Should the SDK name in examples be @redwood/inference or redwood-inference? (consistency with npm org)
- What is the canonical model to use for quickstart? mini-7b used here as placeholder; confirm cost/latency tradeoffs
- Telemetry export: where do quickstart telemetry events land in prod analytics? create mapping doc (CONFLUENCE-DEVEXP-013)
- Mock server behavior: what subset of streaming behaviour do we need to emulate for sidecar demos?

Notes to reviewer:
This doc is purposely pragmatic and prescriptive — the intent is to reduce cognitive overhead for first-time integrators. Prefer short runnable examples rather than long explanations. We'll iterate on language once the examples are implemented and CI-protected.

Change log:
- 2025-03-12 initial draft (Ava)
- 2025-03-15 added telemetry and rollout sections (Liam)
- 2025-03-18 clarified local mock and sidecar flow (Priya)
